<br />
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Where is Your Treasure<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
11 August 2019<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
A Sermon based upon Hebrews 11:1-3,8-16, Luke 12:32-40,
Isaiah 1:16-17<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Let us begin with prayer. May the words of my mouth and
meditations of all of our hearts be accepted in Your sight, Our Rock and Our
Redeemer!<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
These past weeks have been a roller coaster of emotions
and work for me. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
I travelled with a group from UUCC on a mission trip to
CRST. Statistical data of the Midwest shows the reservation as persistent rural
poverty.  The Lakota people are proud of their heritage but mistrusting
of white man due to decades of neglect, hurt and manipulation. In this
environment, Brian, the founder of Simply Smiles, has managed to set up a
summer camp and community center in La Plant. His group is planning and
building a children’s foster care village adjacent to the camp.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Our mission for this trip was 1) to plan and run (with
Simply Smiles staff and interns) a summer camp for reservation youth and 2) to
begin building this foster-care village.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
There were some great times and experiences with
piggyback rides, hikes, and otherwise, but 40 kids full of energy can be exhausting
after a few hours! <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Of the construction, due to the high winds of South
Dakota, Brian opted to base the structure upon concrete reinforced steel. Each
slab weighs over 400 pounds and took no less than 8 people to move or place
each one. By the end of the week, we were all tired.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Still, the experiences with the youth as well as great
conversations with local activists and elders revealed even more depth to today’s
scripture lessons. The mission helped to put perspective about faith and
treasures - not only on the reservation but I believe in our lives
here.  <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>What is Faith?<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Hebrews defines faith as the assurance of things hoped
for and things not seen. Further, faith is a gift given to us by God – someone
we cannot see. Then again, our eyes can deceive us because we might use the
lenses of our ego to see rather than let God unfold it before us. (We have
talked a bit about this.)<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We want to
deserve rather than giving space for grace.  <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Faith, by itself, is not certainty.  If you are
absolutely certain, then you leave no room for faith to work; you leave no room
to grow. When you leave no room for God to work, we are truly alone.  <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>Faith when we fail.<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
This is especially important when we find ourselves <i>certain</i>
about doom and shame. When we fail is when faith becomes important because
we need someone to encourage us. (I wonder who.) We need reassurance telling us
there is more than failure.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>Faith when we succeed.<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
As well, when things are going well (seeming to go our
direction) is when we should review our faith. We might give thanks for the
good fortune we enjoy, and we can observe those around us struggling. We can offer
support (instead of patronizing). It is a form of that “loving neighbor” thing
that Jesus talks about.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
In fact, we know how easily good fortune can change into
something else… like that doctor’s report: one minute you are healthy and the
next you have cancer; Or one minute your pregnant and next your learn the child
wont survive childbirth; Or a person with years of service finds out the layoff
list includes them; Or when government promises to stay off your land but
arrives to take children out of your tribe; (or when a company wants to build a
leaky pipeline under the river that is water source for <i>6 states plus those
connected the Mississippi</i>.)<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
So faith gives us hope and encouragement to live in the
moment; strength when we need. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>Is Faith Our Treasure?<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
This speaks to what Jesus tells us in Luke. First, Jesus reassures
us with “do not be afraid” but follows with “sell our possessions and give
alms.” (What??!) I am not sure about you, but if someone told me this, I
might be little perplexed… because I like my stuff.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Yet, that might be the key here, it is just
stuff.  I was reminded of this during the last week because my stuff embodies
my materialism – my unnecessary. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
For example, I share this picture of Gandhi’s last
possessions and ask what is here. What is so important in the picture that
these were the last of Gandhi’s possessions.  What about clothes,
jewelry, houses and other things?  Why were they not in this picture?
Let me point out the incense and prayer bowl – perhaps Gandhi treasured
faith.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Do you?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>Where is Your Treasure<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Jesus says “for where your treasure is, there your heart
will be also.”  What exactly is your treasure and what would be in
your last ten things?  Could you condense down to ten? <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Of that last one, our privilege allows us to amass
“treasures” for ourselves, and we like to keep stuff for
ourselves.  Yet, I remind you that you are talking about stuff; stuff
that can and does often collect dust – and will not follow you into the
afterlife. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Maybe, we fear scarcity - not having enough or running
out.  I feel like this especially when we have guests where I want to
make sure there is enough for everyone and not run out.  Yet, if you
look at our houses and rooms.  What’s on our walls and around us that
we need to collect more? Inversely, What do we leave behind in the store or on
Amazon if we do not buy it? <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Is this really how we measure our personal
worth?  Is that where our heart is?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
I did this exercise with Stephen ministers, and we asked
ourselves if we could whittle to just ten things. When all said and done, some held
pictures of loved ones, childhood storybooks or mementos of achievements. You
can imagine your special keepsake.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Of those ten things, to put this in perspective of those in
poverty or homeless, what if that was <i>all</i> you had? Even more, what if
someone took those things from you? <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
You may feel violated, angry, defeated or
cheated.  You may cry and wonder “why me?”<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
I think this is where Hebrews lesson is important.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Again, the epistle encourages us to keep the faith even
when the world feels foreign and hostile.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
When the world has us down, faith is where we can turn.
Even when the world gives us yet another shooting, faith is there for us – not
just to believe but as a gift – because in those trying moments, we need real
treasure when empty promises and material just don’t cut it. Faith is real,
tangible and not empty. Faith is there for us, to comfort us, to give us hope, and
to help us believe in something bigger than just us.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Yet, faith does not tell us where we are going to go or
what is going to happen, but faith is letting God reveal those gifts to us - not
relying upon earthly materials.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>Children Can Teach Us about Hope.<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
It is amazing how well laughter of a child can open
hearts and smiles.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>It is amazing how
giggly kid on my shoulders can bring a smile even when hiking up a large hill. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
On the reservation, I saw some of my own childhood
reflected in the youth.  I recognized familiar language, clothes and habits.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Youth have uncanny ability to reveal what
happens or what is said at home. The phrase “the apple doesn’t fall far
from the tree” fits.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
As well, youth are amazing in resilience with ability to
turn bad situations into opportunities – or just fun. They have not etched
their lives in the concrete of adulthood. All I have to remember is how many
people have been in lower class struggle and made it out – of this I can speak
of my own experience. We did not have much, but I believed there was something
more than where I was. That hope is real treasure beyond the material or lack
of. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
It however is a question of what we value as treasure and
what we do with the gifts we have. We have seen people that take their gifts,
horde them, and become greedy for more (like taking treaty land from the
tribes) – because someone thinks they deserve these.  The question is what
are we going to do with the gifts and treasures we have – not just the material
ones?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<b>Faith breeds hope; Faith fulfills the promise.<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
When I think about the youth on reservation, (yes I saw memories,
and) I also saw the hope and possibilities. This gave me more hope for our
wider global youth (not just those on the reservation) – that we can trust them
– we can have faith in them.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
In fact, when I think about it; even when people seem
resigned to depression or oppression, they can and do find hope through
faith. How? If we reach into our childhood for a glimpse of hope and
promise, faith is right alongside. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
My physical youth may be gone, but there is still a child
inside. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Maybe, that is the child in us (perhaps healing) but with
hope, with promise and with dreams. Maybe, that is the child in us that Jesus
calls upon to grow our faith as our real treasure.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Maybe, it was the child inside the elders and activists that
showed a determined faith in what they did as well as showed the people they are.  They
want something more for the younger generations than what they
had.  They were not concentrated on what they could see, but upon the
promise – that which cannot be seen.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
That might sound similar to Abraham since he put faith in
the promise: the God that he could not see. God prepared a way for him and
Sarah because they just wanted a child. They had faith in God to give them that
hope, that child. God gave them (and you) the promise.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
Maybe, that is what we need today. Look for your treasure
in your faith. Your faith breeds hope. That child inside you lives in hope and
promise. Let the promise be fulfilled; then you won’t have to whittle
possessions because that treasure is all you need. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
So is your treasure where your heart is?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<span style="color: #222222;">Thanks Be to God.</span><o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNoSpacing">
<br /></div>
<!--EndFragment--><br /></div>

posts.title: Mystery Revealed - Colossians 1:15-28
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Colossians 1:15-28 unveils the mystery hidden for ages — Christ in you, the hope of glory. Drawn alongside Genesis 18 and Luke 10:38-42, this sermon explores what it means to receive and embody that revealed mystery in daily life.

<br />
Mystery
Revealed<br />
<div class="MsoNormal">
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">A
Sermon based upon Colossians 1:15-28, Genesis 18:1-10, Luke 10:38-42, Psalm 15<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Let
us begin with prayer. May the words of my mouth and meditations of all of our
hearts be accepted in Your sight, Our Rock and Our Redeemer!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">3<sup>rd</sup> Dan Testing<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Many moons ago, I was in Ames testing for my 3<sup>rd</sup> Dan
and it was a challenging event as it pushed my limits.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>It was almost amazing that I was even there
as I had spent the last couple years with a series of knee injuries that
sidelined me.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Finally, I was promoting
to 3<sup>rd</sup> degree.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Things were
going ok and then they asked the group to executing running jump sidekicks, and
I was not sure If I wanted to do much jumping. Yet, I made it this far so why
not? What happens next was something I had not expected.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Elements of a Mystery<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I have always enjoyed watching and reading courtroom dramas and
mysteries, like Scooby Doo. In each of these, writers attempt to present puzzle
for us to try to solve and tossing out clues along the way. Often to make it
interesting, we are given a ruse or red herring, and we are invited to take the
bait that takes into a plausible resolution.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">In fact, I was in a seminar with a magician and he described the
idea that trick of illusionists is to tell you what he will do (like how he was
going to get a dollar bill into an orange) and have your ponder on the
how.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Meanwhile, his attempt is to
sidetrack your attention onto something completely different. Our focus is upon
the tangent regardless of how important the tangent is.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>For instance, we like to focus upon Scooby
Doo and Shaggy antics, while Velma and crew figure out the mystery. When the
big reveal happens, we are amazed at the illusion before us and skill of the
illusionist.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">The Shiny<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">In either case, the writer or performer is intentionally
attempting to divert attention onto those tangents or red herrings.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We love to pay attention to shiniest thing
and the newest thing.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>In our minds we
also like to start making connections to these shiny things and ideas. This
works in our favor with curiosity to learn and discover new things, but it can
also be way to distract us from fundamental truths.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<i><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Dictators take this idea to an extreme. They work to distract us
from a truth, and then there are many possibilities of directing the narrative.
Often by pandering to neglected nostalgia, dictators can fuel discontent and
divert whole societies away from truths.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>When they get enough people to buy into the diversion, they can then use
mob mentality to produce peer pressure into accepting claims as truth by
leaning or conniving to insight personal ego and nostalgia.. This is maybe one
reason why so many Germans felt unaware of the atrocities around them in the
30s and 40s. <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Wrong Conclusions<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">What is the reaction when the big reveal is not what we thought?
(Oh that’s not fair, you didn’t play by the rules, trying to be cute with
intelligence.) When it doesn’t go our way,<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>we can laugh it off, or we might double down - rejecting that we were
misled or fooled. We may even invent facts that corroborate with our version.
We might get mad at the writer/ performer when the big reveal does not align
with our version of the story.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>When that
happens, we might want to check our ego.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I guarantee most of the performers are not out to insult us or
make us look like fools, but magic and mystery shows are not the only places where
we reach wrong conclusions. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Right now vs Right one.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">When an idea looks stale and boring, or we get tired of waiting
for what we think we deserve, we might then switch to instant gratification. We
settle for right now instead of the right one. The goofy thing about that is
how the right one has likely been there the whole time, but we blind ourselves
in one way or another from it.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">We busy ourselves with the right now and live into that idea
regardless of the house of cards we create.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>If we don’t check our ego, we are willing to defend that house of cards
as valid instead of a ruse. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">In Colossians.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">This is what is kind of happening in Colossae. Remember, the
letter is written as an encouragement to keep the faith and to help understand
what Jesus has done for us and what God is doing now.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>The letter encourages us to live servants of
the Gospels and let it inspire us rather than looking for something else –
which is apparently a chief concern for people in Colossae and us as well.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Divine Mystery<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">People are looking for God then and now. Yet, God has revealed
and continues to reveal “riches of the glory of this mystery…” What is this
mystery and what are the riches?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I would avoid thinking only of these “riches” as earthly wealth
or money.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>God is much more than that
because God’s mystery reveals riches of spirit, hope, wisdom, and healing. <span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Jesus made the ultimate sacrifice for us so that we might have
forgiveness and is why the letter expresses the supremacy of Christ. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">So yes, God does mysterious things even now as we sit here.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>God is not just aloof in the sky or only
available once a week in these walls.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>God
is glory! God is hope! God is love! God is in our hearts – waiting for us!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">We only tap into that goodness and let the great mystery live
through us. God is working and speaking. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Maybe you imagined and expected to see God in white long beard
with great royal robe upon a throne. Well, I am sorry to disappoint you – you
got me today. Still, I want to know what you were doing before you got here !<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">God’s Mystery is Working<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I submit to you that God is here and working. If you look deep
into your heart and let God transform you, then you may see God in many forms,
many ways and you may be inspired to lift up and shout out – that You have felt
the Lord; that You have witnessed the Lord!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Yes you may feel that tickle, hear that whisper. You may smell
the aroma and you may see God!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">As we talked last time, you may see God in your neighbor
wherever they are on life’s journey. You may witness God in the space
between.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>You may experience God in your
heart. That experience can be amazing when you let God be in you – not just a
nostalgic image.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">God is near you – perfectly mysteriously – perfectly all the
time.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Yes we may busy ourselves with the shiny moments and our
plausible theories to occupy our minds and time. Then, we miss God working in
those same moments. So I suggest, the next time you are looking around for some
help or some company that God is right there and always has been.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>God is here and in our community and the
mystery is there to discover on God’s time rather than our own. As Garth Brooks
sings, “Some God’s greatest gifts are unanswered prayers.”<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">So let go of the red herring theory, let go of the nostalgia,
let go of the expectation, let go of ego, and let God be with you now.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Let God show you the wonder of this world.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Let God abide in you and bear that fruit of the covenant: the
covenant of love.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">There, the mystery abides and may be revealed when you open your
heart and mind to God as is.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Kicking in Faith<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">So when I executed the flying side kick, something happened that
I did not expect. I jumped the highest that I had ever jumped while executing
the kick. I was so high that two things happened. 1) I triggered my internal
fear of heights (even while being amazed), and 2) I almost landed on the judges
table in front of me.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>This technique was
meant for foot infantry and peasants to be able to kick cavalry riders off
their horses – and now I understand. One of my fellow class mates snapped a
picture of this and suggests that I could have cleared a standing person.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">How did this happen?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">The ego inside me, of course, says that, indeed, I did this!<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Then, I think back to all that I went through
to get to that point. I think of all the people that have been part of that
journey, encouraging me and challenging me to be better – in all of the
training I had done.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>I think of the
times when I was injured and praying for healing: Praying for just a sign.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>God was there always, and these were all clues.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">God guides us in ways that we do not realize.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>No illusions given but God does offer clues
and speaks to us.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">God encouraged you and I to keep the discipline and continues to
bless us.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">So yes our ego can cover our eyes with illusions, but God is wanting
to reveal that mystery and that blessing to us.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>If you let God instead of your expectations of God, then I submit your
possibilities are limitless.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We don’t
have to settle for right now because the right one is right here! When you let
God lift you, then you might reach heights you have never seen. Yes that can be
scary, but very exciting!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">When you let God, then you might witness the mystery revealed.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Thanks Be to God.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<!--EndFragment--><br /></div>

posts.title: Bearing Fruit - Colossians 1:1-14
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Paul's letter to the Colossians opens with a prayer for fruitfulness, paired with Deuteronomy's call to obedience and the parable of the Good Samaritan. The sermon explores what it means to bear fruit in daily life, trusting that God's presence empowers us through fear and failure.

<br />
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Bearing
Fruit<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">A
Sermon based upon Colossians 1:1-14, Deuteronomy 30:9-14, Luke 10:25-37, Psalm 25:1-10<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Let
us begin with prayer. May the words of my mouth and meditations of all of our
hearts be accepted in Your sight, Our Rock and Our Redeemer!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">The
Young Student<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">First
a story about a young student testing for promotion in TKD - asked to break a
board. She looked at the board and the holder with serious apprehension and
looked around scared. I am sure she could describe to you how the board looked
big and menacing to her. I as the holder said, “you can do this.” She lifted up
her leg and bam - nothing broke. Then a second time, same thing . Then, I said
to her, “pause and breathe we are with you and not against you.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Go through the board – don’t meet it. You can
do this!” Other people offered words of encouragement as well. She collected
herself, set, lifted her leg, bam and through the board she went. She looked
with astonishment and jumped at her accomplishment while the room applauded.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="color: black; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Sometimes,
we just need some encouragement that we are doing the right thing - that people
see or recognize the effort, and our lectionary today gives us some of that.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Our epistle today comes from Colossians, and this is written as
a strong encouragement for that community (and ours) to continue to be
faithful.  This encouragement is done with prayer and the image of <i>bearing
fruit</i> is core to this message.  So what does “bearing fruit” mean? (I
am glad you asked, and to help this...) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">One theologian remarks that one cannot read the epistles without
digging into the other parts of the scripture, and this lesson is a perfect
example of that.  Our lectionary offers some specific examples and takes us through Torah law in Deuteronomy
with “God will make you abundantly prosperous in all your undertakings, in the
fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your soil…”
The lectionary also takes us to the story of the Samaritan in Luke with a fellow offering much needed comfort
to someone in distress. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">How do these texts inform us as to what this letter to Colossae
says about <i>bearing fruit</i>?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Deuteronomy Fruit.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Of Deuteronomy, the scripture reminds that command in the Torah
is to do the good work of God with all your heart and all your soul. This calls
to our familial, growth, agricultural and ecological fruitfulness traits. (We
could go further into Genesis with this and observe “be fruitful and multiply.”
) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">This however could be misconstrued to expect a certain <i>kind</i>
of prosperity as reward. (Besides prosperity for a single person might be
different than a person, like me with a family.) Prosperity can be defined in
so many ways – not just money. So what kind of reward is God mentioning in
Deuteronomy.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">The fruit may be an allusion to the covenantal relationship as
the gifts of God that permeates all parts of our lives – not just at worship.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Last time I was here, we talked about justification by faith and
daring greatly to live our faith and this portion of Deuteronomy roots our faith,
our justification and our prosperity in good works of (oh oh oh not you or me
but God). <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">That leads us to the Gospels.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">DOC General Assembly - Abide as Fruit<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I should note here that Des Moines will be hosting DOC version
of GS this coming weekend.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Their theme comes
from John 15 where Jesus refers to being “the vine… and those who abide in me
and I in them bear much fruit.” Thus, this fruit again talks about covenant: to
love God and to love our neighbor “with whole heart and soul.”<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>You ask who is my neighbor? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Summary of the Samaritan.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Another great because in Luke, Jesus was asked the same
question.  Jesus provides us a lesson (a parable) of a Samaritan in Luke
where two people were given a chance to help a person in need.  A priest
and a Levite, people of privilege and duty, walked along the other side of the
road and who did not, could not and would not be bothered to help.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">When a particular Samaritan arrives, he sees the traveler and
moves to help – the Samaritan sees (<b><u>sees</u></b>) while the others
ignored. The Samaritan is moved to help - without knowing the details about the
traveler.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Seeing the Invisible.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I have remarked about my work with UBFM in our work with area homeless.
In these interactions, one thing the Spirit teaches us is the value and dignity
of every single human being. For so long in my life, I would simply walk by and
not even know there was person sitting on the park bench.  For so long, I
would drive by an overpass and not realize that someone has been living in the
crevice for the last couple months. (Maybe you are nodding because you
recognize your behavior.) For so long, I just did not see… <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">We could deliberate for a long time why we do this.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">In the face of that, I submit that the Holy Spirit works magic, and that
can yield unexpected and remarkable changes our lives.  You can no longer
un-see, and you might suddenly realize how beautiful your own life is with wonders,
privileges and joys in the midst of our own brokenness, bills, worries – when
you are willing to see. This is not necessarily a sense of righteous pride but
realizing the privileges that we have been afforded are things we could lose.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Seeing is Mutually Beneficial<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I can tell you stories about some of these encounters where the
sustenance we provided was received with joyful tears of honest, grateful
blessings upon us in turn.  While they were appreciating the food and
supply, one thing I feel is that we seeing them instead of looking away or
ignoring is the important part.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">As someone who studies martial arts and self-defense, this is
two-fold. Seeing means I recognize who is in my environment, but seeing people
is recognizing God’s child<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>and God’s
creation right there in some actually interesting and subtle beauty.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">We don’t hand out money but when I do see a person on a corner
holding a sign -- I no longer quickly turn up the windows or hastily look busy
trying not to make eye contact. I, at least, acknowledge they are there – and
that can be powerful for each of us.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">I know some people and media like to paint a picture that these people
are just manipulating our good emotions, but I guarantee you people are in real
distress all around our community. And all God’s children deserve to be treated
with dignity rather than ignored. Go ahead and say hi!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">That is where the Samaritan is important because this person
crossed culture lines and walls of society but gave no question of condition
for giving comfort – like a good caregiver  would do. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Bearing Witness<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">So these texts reminds us of our covenant to God and our
neighbor and compel us to see our neighbor – and does not put conditions on
that. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">That brings us back to our epistle. Another way to read
Colossians is in parallel where bearing fruit is bearing witness.  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">When we witness the suffering (whether racial injustice, kids in
cages at the border, Native Americans having water rights stolen from them,
shaming or bullying), are we moved to help? -- because that is what God is
calling us to do. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">That seeing might make us uncomfortable and uneasy, but loving
God and the rewards of that Spirit call us to do the good Christian work
“daring greatly” even when it makes us uncomfortable.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">It could be easy for us to quietly brush aside someone’s hurt as
someone else’s issue or when we defiantly refuse to see what is happening… We
are forgetting the command we have been given – to love God and our neighbor
with our whole heart. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">What if it was you?<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">You could even flip the roles. What if you were put in a
position where you felt like you had no one to help you, the system fails you,
or people were constantly avoiding the systemic problems while calling it “good.”<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>You might be a little annoyed and would you
feel hurt. (Our theme from General Synod is to be the seasoning and to light
the world with God’s love, less we are tasteless and buried from sight.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>)<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<b><span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Transformative power of God<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Thus, we are called into service, we can “dare greatly”, and we
can “rise strong” in our faith. That starts with us seeing and witnessing the
power of God and light in the children of God that are all around us. We can
see the blessings of humanity in all the nooks and crannies of our lives, the
world. <b><u>There</u></b>, we will see God at work.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">When we see and we witness God working, then our lives and our
hearts can be transformed by the mighty power of God. Then no one will be able
to put out your light or that of others because you felt love of God deep in
your heart. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">We can be rescued from the power of evil and transform into the
full power of grace, faith and hope. That becomes contagious in good way. 
Wouldn’t that be nice? To see a whole community moved to be and do the graceful
work of God (rather than be consumed by division and hate because we refused to
see.)  All it takes is just one act to start – to see, to bear fruit, and to
bear witness.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">When the TKD student felt encouraged and in community with us, then
she witnessed what she could do, and she lit up and filled the whole room with
her joy!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Lift up your eyes, bear fruit, bear witness to the light, bear
witness to God, bear witness to your neighbor (no matter where they are on
life’s journey) and be moved to mercy with love, compassion and faith.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Then, you may be filled with spiritual wisdom and understanding
as you share that witness with our neighbors – near and far. Then together, we
can all lift up God’s grace, and bear fruit that God has blessed us all, as
children of God, with these wonderful gifts with all your heart and all your
soul.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="background: white;">
<span style="color: #222222; mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-fareast-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Thanks Be to God.</span></div>

posts.title: Spirit of the Living God - Pentecost Jun 9 2019
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Acts 2:1-21 and Romans 8:14-17 anchor this Pentecost sermon on the Spirit of the Living God. Using Iowa vs. Iowa State football rivalry as a relatable opening, the preacher explores how the Spirit forms and unites a diverse community of faith.

<div class="MsoNormal">
Spirit of the Living God<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">A Sermon based upon Acts 2: 1-21, John 14:27, Psalm 104, and
Romans 8:14-17<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let us begin with prayer. May the words of my mouth and
meditations of all of our hearts be accepted in Your sight, Our Rock and Our
Redeemer!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Happy Pentecost!  One of the high holy holidays of our
faith!  Congratulations to our youth on their awesome confirmation!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Today, I present to you a couple stories to talk about the Spirit
of the Living God.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">IOWA vs ISU<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The first story is a familiar one to Iowans. Picture it, it is the second Saturday of
September and a train of cars are heading to Ames or Iowa City for the Iowa vs Iowa State
football game. You know that my house is a house divided. So I am not going to
tell you what is or isn’t correct about the best team on that field that day.
What happens is interesting experience for all involved.  We witness
people on both sides cheering and having great time before the game.  It
moves to anxiety and nervousness as game progresses with prayers being lofted
left and right for just the right pass or just the right fumble.  Then when the final is recorded, fans are either completely
overjoyed or in complete misery. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Was the spirit working for one side of prayers versus the
other?  I submit to you that God is not just on one side no matter how
good your curl at the end zone.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Despite winning or going home disappointed and hurt, God happens
on both sides. God is comforting and connecting communities through the Spirit.
If you look closely, you may even see God bridging the divide because God wants
us to lift us – God wants us, not just some of us.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This leads me to my next story.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">UBFM God Moments<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">God happens within and around the group and<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">With the people that we serve by teaching us that all deserve dignity
& respect.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The next story is about a group that I am involved in Des Moines called UBFM. We provide an "extravagant welcome one burrito at a
time." Every Thursday, a number of us gather in the basement of a church to put
together supplies, sandwiches and burritos for homeless people around the
metro. Then we are sent out on bike and car routes to deliver
said gifts.  Before that, our leader does a safety briefing before
sending people out. Each time, we are asked about God moments.  </span><br />
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;"><br /></span>
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">You ask, what are those? When people find some positive development in a regular
“client” or we just hear something positive, these are usually raised as God
moments. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There are times when there is none that are obvious, but I submit
there is something happening right then and there - always. God is working in the group
- in the preparations, the conversations, and the delivery.  People may
not be aware when the spirit is working, but I have become accustomed to seeing
the spirit working in that group.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">UBFM may not be a formal church in our work, but God is working
through them and in every interaction with the people we serve.  The
Spirit is not just working within the group but those we serve as their faces
light up when we show up. The Spirit is teaching us that every person on their
place in life’s journey wants and deserves basic dignity and respect, and those
people will sometimes gift us a prayer. That is truly moving.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Spirit works during success and our desperate hours.<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">You see, the Spirit works for us in many good ways during success or
victory, and even in our most desperate hour (just like with the homeless, or
the losing side of the game). The Spirit is working, nudging, tickling,
comforting and just being amazing. The Spirit is working even, as our youth remind
us, if we are not listening. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The key is that the <b><u>spirit is working</u></b>, and all we
have to do is <b><u>listen</u></b> -- <b><u>give it time</u></b>. </span><br />
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;"><br /></span>
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Some might
say the spirit is in our faith.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Faith of Our Youth<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I enjoyed working with the youth these past couple weeks and
congrats to the leaders for their tremendous work! You are all to be
commended!<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>The youth showed courage today, and their statement of faith reminds us that the Spirit lives though their
example. So have some faith in our youth because they showed faith in the Holy Spirit!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let the Spirit Work: Confessional<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">While we might want to overlook or forget (or it just feels hard), the spirit is working in our midst. In daily living, I admit and
confess that sometimes I just wander away and forget but why? <o:p></o:p></span><br />
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;"><br /></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">It is because I let something get in the way, or I did not let God.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">So, You, yes You!  Have faith; have spirit. Let it work for you. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Because:<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The Holy Spirit expresses and reveals our community and God at
work together.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The Holy Spirit expresses our hopes and aspirations while bringing
us closer to the One because as Romans says, we are children of God led by the
Spirit of God. So let us witness that spirit because God is grace and glory!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">  <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Give time in your daily lives to hear and see God at work because
as St Paul writes, “now is the acceptable time.” In the moments of life, (e.g.
prayer, trial, and success,) we can find God and that beautiful spirit.  If
we just step back and breathe a moment, the Spirit is right there – next to
your heart and soul. In this way, we can find that Spirit. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yes, Now is the time.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Being the Example<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Remember always, Jesus commands us to love God and to love our
neighbor.  With this command, we can not only, experience the Spirit, but we
can be an example of the Spirit working. We can be the example of that
compassion during hard times like floods, tornados, loss, victory, and just
decent humanity of acknowledging someone is there – not forgotten. We work
through the Spirit of Christ in us. So, embody that Spirit for our community
and all the great good that can happen.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yes Now is the Time for that Spirit of God!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Wine @ 9:00?<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The disciples were asked if they were filled with wine before
9:00. By our clock, it is just after 10:00. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The question should have been, are you filled with the Holy Spirit?
If you were full of the Spirit, others might think you had enough wine too.
 It makes you act funny, goofy, and happy. When you give it time to fill you, it
opens you up, releases you from burdens, moves you, comforts you and grooves
with you. Then you may find the spirit of the living God descend upon you.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Whether at a sports contest, during mission work, being sick,
being homeless, being queer, saying prayer or just being alive… The spirit
might be like having wine at the 10:00 hour.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Be filled with the peace that Jesus gives,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">be filled with grace, comfort and hope.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The Spirit is working. Just look at the wonderful around you! And
inside you!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Isnt that just awesome!?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yes Now is the Time for that Spirit of God!<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">This is Pentecost – Be filled with peace -- be filled with the
Spirit in you!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Thanks Be to God.</span></div>

posts.title: Woe to contentment (Lenten Journeys Luke13 and Luke6)
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Luke 13:31-35 and Psalm 27 anchor this Lenten reflection on the danger of spiritual complacency. The sermon calls congregants out of contentment and into the ongoing, unfinished work of faithful discipleship.
