<span style="font-family: "helvetica";">Coming
Home</span><br />
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">10
June 2018 <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: 14.0pt; mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">A reflection based upon Ezekiel 2:1-5 • Psalm 123 • 2
Corinthians 12:2-10 • Mark 6: 1-13<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: 14.0pt; mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<u style="text-underline: #0C63C1;"><span style="color: #0c63c1; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;"><a href="https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Samuel%208:4-11,%20(12-15),%2016-20,%20(11:14-15);Genesis%203:8-15;Psalm%20138;Psalm%20130;2%20Corinthians%204:13-5:1;Mark%203:20-35"><span style="color: #0c63c1;">Link to Scriptures</span></a></span></u><span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: 14.0pt; mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Will you pray with me? May the words of my mouth
and the meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your sight O Lord, our Rock,
Our Redeemer.  Amen.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: 14.0pt; mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Our
text from the Gospel of Mark tells us a familiar story of homecoming. It is a
homecoming accompanied with a stubborn rejection of one’s acquired knowledge
and skills.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">There
are many stories that I could think that are relative to this situation. When I
came home from college full of new passions and newfound understanding, I just
wanted to share with everyone.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>The
reception was kind of neeah, “we love ya Tony, but we know ya.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Those
who go on a retreat may come back to a lukewarm reception as well. Soldiers
returning from overseas understand this dilemma full well. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">You
see, while we have been growing and learning on our personal journey, the rest
of home have went about life business as usual without so much as an occasional
burp. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We may
have returned from a good journey full of newfound knowledge and hot passions,
but everyone we know also remembers who we were before we left (aka the good, the
bad, and the ugly.) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">In
these experiences of being on journeys, even our friends and family may not
realize what has changed in us or why that is important to us. These
circumstances invoke the adage, “familiarity breeds discontent” because people,
over time, become complacent and inert to change -- even when that change may
be literally what the doctor ordered. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We
have become accustomed to the way things are rather than worrying about what
they should be.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>(No one likes to worry
so I can understand.) Yet, We have allowed injustice and misery to become
normal to us rather than speaking out or even truly living our faith.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We have become accustomed to living something
different than living the truth : <span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> </span>we all
belong to community and that we are all deserving of grace. Some even cry foul
when our brothers and sisters come to their senses and ask for their rightful
part of equality and liberty.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">This
return from our recent ascent <span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> </span>and
journey invokes the inertia because we have changed the dynamic of our being,
but the familiar routine has not changed. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Question
is, why allow inertia to rule us? Why allow inertia to take away God-given
rights and happiness from ourselves or our neighbors?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Inertia
is resistance to change, and yes, we will find that resistance in those closest
to our hearts because small or big change disrupts the routines. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">No
matter how good our intentions, or how hot our passions, humanity enjoys
routines and thus resists change. (I understand this as I enjoy being able to
sit and relax once in a while.)<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>What if
the doctor says we have to get up and do exercise, stop drinking, stop smoking,
or eat differently, is that when we should invoke inertia? So when the wisdom
of Jesus tells us to love for our neighbors, do we just ignore<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>like we do the doctor?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Sometimes,
this “change” could be simply asserting what is already there, like boundaries.
Perhaps, we have allowed people to cross our boundaries, push us around or
ignore our thoughts. Perhaps, we have allowed society to ignore our fundamental
rights and allowed apathy towards oppression of brothers and sisters. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Complacent
people get so used to living with oppression and with injustice. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Change
may simply be saying “I have had enough.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We may
feel that we are called to action, and yes, many may not share that enthusiasm.
Our scriptures tell of the sending of the disciples to remind us there are
people willing to share this enthusiasm when we are willing to go out and find
them. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">There
are people out there right now that need help, need hope and yearning for a
path.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Life, liberty and pursuit of
happiness is being threatened all around us.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We
need to be awake to the plight of our brothers and sisters whether it is racial
injustice, immigrant family separation or gender inequality. We do not have to
blindly accept when society wants to take what little we have or to force us
into something we are not.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Maybe
it is time for us to say, “I have had enough.”<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">I have
seen this journey because it took decades of worry, hope and work to get to the
place we are today. I am watching our world dismantle the love and grace that
our country can be into a sweltering pot of anxiety and hostility. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">When
people get singled out like is happening to immigrants today (for doing nothing
more than trying to make good homes), justice suffers and the love of God is
being ignored.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>What are we teaching our
next generations about love and justice? That exclusion is ok and the hate is
God’s way?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">If we
say nothing, and let the injustice rule today, it is only a matter of time
before they start knocking on the doors of other Americans and telling them to
get into the boxcars and the concentration camps? Will inertia rule that day?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We may
do the right thing and have learned valuable truths, but sharing that wisdom to
people unwilling to receive it is like throwing the good news in a fire.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Maybe people are suspicious or a bit jealous,
but we cannot let them burn the love of God, that is we cannot let them burn
what’s good in us, in the fire of hate and discontent.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Yes
Maybe it is time for us to say, “I have had enough.”<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<i><span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">For
those not ready to receive wisdom, this sharing may appear to be trickery and
nonsense since the wisdom may not conform to our (valid or invalid)
perceptions. When we play the role of truth teller, being a prophetic voice can
be difficult.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Injustice
is happening and boundaries are being crossed. We cannot ignore the
reality.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We cannot let the service and
sacrifice of so many of our honorable go in vain. They served and sacrificed
for an ideal greater than themselves that is liberty and justice for all. Let
that not be in vain. We must be willing to be love and justice.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We
must be willing seek out God’s love and justice in our own hearts and minds.
Then we will find recipients of that love and justice when we share the story
of our journey just as Paul does with Corinth.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Paul
reminds us that wisdom starts with personal trials and lessons, and we should
share our passion so long as we lift up our friends and families experiences in
them. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">God’s
love and justice needs a friend in these times. We cannot risk more inertia to
the suffering of our brothers and sisters. Say no to harmful injustice to our
communities.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">We
know that we are broken and have failed, but our failure does not have to continue.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We are much more than that. Together, we are
blessed to be the goodness of love and justice that unites our community.
Together, we believe in the good that we are.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>Together, we grow to share love with children and families of white
people, immigrants, black people, LGBT people, Native Americans and many more. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Real
wisdom, passion and justice are right around the corner for our use. God is
ready to light our passion and bring us together.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal" style="mso-layout-grid-align: none; text-autospace: none;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "helvetica"; mso-bidi-font-family: Helvetica;">Thanks
Be to God.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<!--EndFragment--><br />

posts.title: When We Fail - Mark 3
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Drawn from 1 Samuel 8, Psalm 138, 2 Corinthians 4:13–5:1, and Mark 3:20-35, this reflection explores what happens when people fail — from Israel's demand for a king to the scribes' accusations against Jesus. The sermon traces how failure and forgetting shape communities, and what grace looks like in response.

<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When We Fail<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">10 June 2018 <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">A
reflection based upon 1 Samuel 8 • Psalm 138 • 2 Corinthians 4:13-5:1 • Mark 3:20-35<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span class="MsoHyperlink"><span style="font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"><a href="https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=1%20Samuel%208:4-11,%20(12-15),%2016-20,%20(11:14-15);Genesis%203:8-15;Psalm%20138;Psalm%20130;2%20Corinthians%204:13-5:1;Mark%203:20-35">Link
to Scriptures</a></span></span><span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Will
you pray with me? May the words of my mouth and the meditations of our
hearts be acceptable in your sight O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer.  Amen.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There are a couple themes that are prominent in these
darker texts today. We could talk about the failure of people in 1 Samuel or we
could talk about the token villains of Mark’s Gospel in the scribes. How are
these related ? One theologian suggests that 1 Samuel kind of sets up the
problem in the Gospel of Mark. <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">What
do we do when we fail.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>In Samuel, the
people fail to remember the experience of the tyrant pharaoh and demand a new
“king”. In Mark, the scribes fail (or refuse) to see God at work in Jesus. Even
Jesus fails to persuade the intolerant scribes of this.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Ever have that happen to you?<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Ever walk into a conversation or event
thinking I am going to wow them only to be totally rejected.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>You walk away with mixed emotions: hurt,
distrust, and even some anger. How could they be so blind as to not see the
Truth?<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I
kind of understand the dilemma that falls upon Jesus as I have had similar experiences.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Jesus goes before the elders to make a case about
Gods work and what the mission of God means.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>Perhaps, Jesus expected a fair hearing of his testimony, but instead, he
is condemned by the elders.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>He is sent
out of the meeting linking wounds. <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">Subsequently,
Jesus knows that his mission lays not in that religious institutions.<o:p></o:p></i></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Through
their rejection of Jesus, the scribes actually prefer human power and tradition
over the transformative and restorative power of God’s work and God’s love
today. I have witnessed this kind of rejection from the Church, and it causes
one to question the whole idea of Church. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Church
is run by people, and like all human institutions, they are fallible (I
included).<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yet
we are called to God’s work. It is up to us to speak against injustices like
slavery, destruction of Native American people or the exclusion of LGBT because
we, as Christians, must speak for all of God’s children, no matter where they
are on life’s journey. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We
are called to church because church is a place of good and hope. We can find the
community of God here. Through God, we can find liberation, restoration,
forgiveness and true grace. We have to be willing to see it, grab it, hug it,
and to hold on to it because God’s love can take us for an awesome ride. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Failure
can be our greatest teacher: when we let it teach us. Here, we acknowledge our
brokenness, imperfection, and need for providence. We may even witness God at
work during that failure-- working to teach us something. We have to be willing
to listen<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>and be willing to let the
moment be a teaching one rather than to perpetuate wrongdoing (aka mask with a
flimsy excuse or worse.) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">If
you lie to yourself, are you helping yourself or causing yourself more problems?
People may end up believing in our own lies because they never accepted our
failure. That can lead down the path they call the “unforgivable.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">If
we poison our minds with delusions of power, false righteousness or believe our
false excuses, then we risk losing the connection to the greater power of God
and the community. If we consume ourselves<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>with our own desires and interests like a narcissist, we leave no room
for true enlightenment and grace that could build us. Thus, if we keep going
down that path, as to be unredeemable, we may forsake all the real good and
real potential that is around us -- the real love that binds our community.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">These
are moments in life that teach us about human fallibility whether an
institution or us as a person, and still God is there to lift us and forgive
us. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Our
love binds us and moves us forward throughout all of this.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>That is a point of the last part of our
Gospel when Jesus reminds us of the value of our connections as family. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Families,
or our real connections, become important to us when all else does not seem to
go our way. When we are rejected, we go to those closest to us for
reassuring.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>In those moments, we
Question like What did I do wrong even though I did nothing wrong?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We
know that when we face rejection and obstacles we turn to those we trust: our
family (not just family of blood).<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Our “families”
in life turn out to be those that share life, breath, joys, concerns and pains.
That is where we may find the restoration and liberation of God right here on Earth:
that in our best friends. They believe in us and lift us when we need that help,
just like God. If you look closely, you just might witness God in them. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">So
despite our best efforts, intentions and ignorance, we fail. We have to get
back up and keep going. We just reach out and God will be there waiting for us
--to restore us and renew us. In the midst of summer celebrations and parades,
these scriptures remind us to be penitential when we do wrong, recognize when
good happens, and to enjoy the graces we get -> and to remember from where
those graces arise.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">In
these penitential verses, there is also a call to remember your family, those
who support you and those in your community. We are all broken, need to heal
and we can begin the healing by forgiving others. We are here for each other
and we can extend a little of the grace in our lives to our family, and our
community. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Then,
we can do the work of liberation and justice called of us by God because we
have God’s grace and forgiveness always. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I
did not realize how personal this sermon could get or how hard it would be to
write. Yet, the message was timely and I was almost crying as I finished up
because I needed a little uplifting.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>As
I wrote, I could look up and smile again as I saw God all around us …restoring
us<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Thanks Be to God.</span></div>

posts.title: What's Your Story - Acts 1
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Acts 1:15-17, 21-26 recounts the choosing of Matthias to restore the circle of twelve apostles, raising questions about roots, foundation, and belonging. The sermon explores what this story means for our own narratives of faith, eternal life, and how we understand our place in God's community.

<br />
What’s Your Story<br />
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">13 May 2018 <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">A
reflection based upon Acts 1:15-17, 21-26 • Psalm 1 • 1 John 5:9-13 • John 17:6-19<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"><a href="https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Acts%201:15-17,%2021-26;Psalm%201;1%20John%205:9-13;John%2017:6-190;src=link">Link
to Scriptures</a><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Will
you pray with me? May the words of my mouth and the meditations of our
hearts be acceptable in your sight O Lord, our Rock, Our Redeemer.  Amen.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">On this seventh Sunday of Easter, Let us walk through a narrative
in this week’s scripture. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We are going to talk about roots, eternal life, and what’s your
story.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The Story
of 12 (Roots and Foundation):<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Our scriptures this week from Acts talks about the one Apostle
that joins the group after a discussion and vote. The question can be raised of
why the need to keep the number as 12.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There is a relationship of the 12 Apostles with the 12 tribes of
Israel. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">The Apostles keep the number 12 by selecting Matthias. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">With that, we are also reminded of the importance of heritage <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because our Church has roots in Jewish traditions and
culture.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Fundamentally, the reminder is not just of our roots, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">but we are reminded not to forget the lessons and the celebrations
of our heritage. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is one reason we read the Old Testament section of the Bible.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is not just a story about God <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">but about our humanity’s lessons, fallibility and celebrations.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">In those books, we faced many obstacles, threats, and destruction.
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We were once objects of persecution, slavery and tyranny <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">– much like our neighbors are today. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We still make mistakes. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">These roots humbly remind us of what impact that has, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and we should work to correct that in our society today. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We also celebrate the many achievements <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because the Creator has been helping us to learn. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">In those many books of the OT, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">lives and stories were shared<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">- so that we don’t forget the lessons. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Let us pray not to forget those lessons today. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Story of
Eternal Life (Future and Legacy):<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Our epistle reading is a synopsis of what Easter season means, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">specifically this “Eternal Life”.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Well, what does “eternal life” mean? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Some may think it refers to the afterlife. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I honestly don’t know what happens on the other side of death <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">--<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>I have not been there, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and I prefer to take my time getting there. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I have images of Heaven. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Thus, Heaven may be waiting for us and for you, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">but what really, can “eternal life” mean for us today. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">What life do we make here? <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We have our life (aka our story) that we share. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">An important word of the epistle is “testimony.” <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There are some interesting origins of the word testimony. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yet, testimony is our witness, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and ultimately, we are telling our story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Through our stories, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we have life and we reveal our connections, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">our community, and our families. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">For example, I can’t tell you about my life without my story <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">just as you cannot without your story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">If we are to be true in our testimony, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">then we must not be afraid of the struggles and questions of our
lives. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Those hard parts are just as important <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because those reveal our humanity and lessons (just like our roots
in the Old Testament)<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">that we have learned along the way. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is part of the prayer of Psalm 1. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">My dad served in Vietnam, and to his grave, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">he would not tell us about many of those experiences. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I have to wonder What could have been learned from his struggle <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and his questions in those stories. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Doing Stephen ministry or pastoral care,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When people tell me their story, even the hard parts, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We have a chance to heal. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Dad’s story lives on from what he did share, but <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Perhaps, he may have learned more by talking about it,<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and I certainly would have better understood the pain and life he
witnessed.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">(I wonder
how many other vets are not able heal because they don’t share their story.)<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is part of our roots.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We live and breathe our experience of the Spirit, community,
success and failure. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Together, we learn to have life and live life; not just as spoken
or written words. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Through our witness, we are examples of that life <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and what Easter means to us <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">even during dire times.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">What are you doing today to let your story live or even live into
your family?<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Your Story
(Wondering the Present):<o:p></o:p></span></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When times feel dire, you may feel hurt, lonely or repressed. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Perhaps, you found joy in life only to see it taken. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Perhaps, the world seems to be full of people that don’t share your
values <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">(or experiences).</i> <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When you feel lost, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Take pause to remember your witness, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">your story <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and who you are. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When I am lost, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I question everything and sometimes, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">my questions simply don’t make sense. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">(I might go visit Mom and talk.) <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">By talking and telling the story, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">things may start to make sense.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">I find myself working out what I have done, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">what I have been taught, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">and what I could have done better.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Somehow, a path unfolds before me <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because I am reminded of how I came to be here today. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We can find ourselves in mediation, prayer and story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Still it sucks to feel lost. Don’t be disappointed.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">From Gospel
John 17, we are reminded that Jesus and the Apostles lived in a time under vicious
oppression and the Bible written when Jerusalem was destroyed by the Romans. <o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Listen to
these words: “And now I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world
and I am coming to you. Holy Father protect them in your name.. so that they
may be one as we are one…I have given them your word and the world has hated
them...I am not asking you to take them out of the world , but I ask you to
protect them.” One theologian uses the Gospel prayer to remind us that
destruction happens and our values are in fact valuable.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">There is
real anguish and experience of loss, but still, we can witness the hope and
reassurance of Jesus. All we have to do is remember what it felt like to watch
the World Trade Center Towers burn and collapse. Whether physical destruction,
getting old or injured, Jesus reminds us of our values and our roots-- That we are
more than just symbols or our past. We came together as community.<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">A path is before us even when we feel alone or lost.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Look up and see the light before you.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Tell your story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Lift up the many experiences around you. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Then, You can reconnect. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We are in a world where we witness and we testify <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">to the grace of God and the Church’s mission. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Yes, I see a world all around me <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">that don’t share my sense of values, my sense of discipline or my
experience. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That’s ok.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Jesus, in John’s Gospel, reminds us<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">that we don’t have to be the same. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Hopefully, we understand <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">identity</i>;
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">that is great because you realize who you are. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">And, in Jesus’s prayer, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we are not here to dictate to others or to fix people.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Wouldn’t that be awesome to have a switch
that we flip and suddenly everything is ok.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"><span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">(I could
lose 30 pounds a lot easier that way!)<o:p></o:p></span></i></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We, first, have to take care of ourselves.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We are commanded by Jesus to be examples of God’s love to each
other and our families. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We share our story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We listen to others tell their story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We are here to share in the community precisely <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">because the community needs our story. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We share our experiences and witness. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Through our story and our example, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we show the value of a good path, including the broken parts. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Then together, we realize that community is belonging to each other
<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">-- not just empty slogans and phrases.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When we pray together, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we eat together, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we work together, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we sing together, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">we fail together, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">then we heal together. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">We fill our community with our testimony in our unique ways<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">—we give life to our community and to us as ourselves.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">When we embody the presence that heals and shares love, <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">that is how we have eternal life and legacy. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is how we honor our roots. <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is how we live today and witness today.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is our roots! <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is life lived! <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is our story! <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">That is the Gospel story! <o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">And I am sticking to it!<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">Thanks Be to God.</span></div>
<br />

posts.title: Bearing Fruit with Love - John 15
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: John 15:1-8, Psalm 22, and 1 John 4:7-21 frame a reflection on bearing fruit through love. The sermon challenges fear and divisiveness, calling the congregation to witness Christ with whole heart and mind.

<br />
Bearing Fruit with Love: How We Conquer Fear and
Divisiveness<br />
<div class="MsoNormal">
<div class="MsoNormal">
<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Tony E Hansen<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
29 April 2018 <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-bidi-font-family: "Times New Roman";">A reflection based upon Psalm 22 • 1 John 4:7-21 • John 15: 1-8<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<span style="mso-bidi-font-family: Calibri; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-latin;">As someone of fitness, I would like to exercise your hearts and
minds today. You may agree with me with things and you may not. Just remember
that some things, like exercise, might make you uncomfortable.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>We know with Christ’s call to service,
discomfort is part of the territory. Like Christ, exercise can help our hearts
get stronger.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>So let us witness Christ
together with whole heart and mind.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div style="line-height: 14.0pt; margin-bottom: .0001pt; margin: 0in;">
<span style="color: black; font-family: "calibri" , sans-serif; mso-bidi-font-family: "Times New Roman";">Will you pray with me? May the words of my mouth and the
meditations of our hearts be acceptable in your sight O Lord, our Rock, Our
Redeemer.  Amen.<o:p></o:p></span></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;">The Issue: Fear and Divisiveness.<o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
For our reflection, I am going to address a difficult issue
that impact our everyday lives today and one that needs our attention. <span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> </span>I want to talk about rampant fear-based
spiritual abuse and divisiveness. We see this in a bunch of places all around
us. We see it on the news, in the halls of government, during the coffee hour,
at the ballpark, and we see it in church: yes from people like you and me. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Why is this issue important and why today? The Gospel of
John likes to talk community and how people belong to the community. Our Gospel
today invokes the imagery of the vine, as interconnectedness, and growing of
the community. Further, the epistle from John provides a way to “cure” the ills
of division and abuse. So let us address the problem, look at the cure, and understand
a path to the cure. Ultimately, that is God’s vision for us, and so, the
question is how do we get there?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
First, in order to correct an injustice or cure a disease (and
disease it is), we must be willing to name it. For centuries, people would treat
mental illness by throwing people into asylums which was the same as a prison
cell. Otherwise, creative relatives might lock up one of their own so as to
hide the issue in the closet, the attic or remote room that was left alone. People
were given cute names (e.g. funny farm, looney bin, crazy house or worse) and
people were warned to stay away like the illness was contagious. Yet, what was
contagious was the fear that people perpetuated. Instead of helping people,
society preferred to simply not deal with the issue and hid behind their own
fears. People watching others in treatment saw how horrible the conditions
were, but did nothing. They were paralyzed by irrationality. Some of the fears
were real but focused upon the symptoms instead of the cause. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Then one day, some people decided, these were real people
with real issues. They called it “depression”, “anxiety” or if you were from
battle, “shell-shocked” (which almost sounds as bad as the explosions
themselves.) They gave it a name decided asylums were in fact not solving the
issue but rather hiding an ugly truth. We have ways to go with mental illness,
but we have come far.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Divisive and Fear spiritual abuse is another illness. Like
depression affects a person, this illness affects our (the whole) community and
is making our community very sick for far too long. We have locked it away
behinds closed doors of secret societies and hypocritical oaths sworn to defend
a “right” to discriminate. We used cute phrases in order to normalize the
sickness like “that’s the way we’ve always done it,” “it’s tradition,” or “they
don’t live like us”, or even better “they deserve God’s wrath.” (and why was it
deserved, I ask?) For doing nothing more than trying to make a peaceful home in
this community – in God’s community.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>What
is important is that language is part of this because the use of “they and
them” in opposition to “us or our” helps us articulate the illusions of
division.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
This is one reason why people have wondered about the Gospel
truths when those that profess them want to demonize many around them. Even
though people simply want an equal and fair part in the community of God, there
have been people sitting in pews and standing in pulpits that say “not for you.”
Where is the Gospel in such a message? How welcoming is that?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
This is one reason why some people do not feel there is a
church home for them. I mean why would anyone want to subject a spouse, let
alone their beloved children, into a space that offers lofty words that all but
hide a sign of hate in their work.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> 
</span>Regardless of writings on the walls or what was read in scriptures, what
people do matters. When people don’t feel welcomed or when they feel conflicted
by what they have heard or experienced, that is spiritual abuse and builds fear
of Church and God.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Our challenge should you choose to accept it. How do we
bring these people back to God? How do we as a community heal? How do we pass
onto our children a church that bears the good fruit today and tomorrow?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;">A Cure <o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
A Cure according to 1<sup>st</sup> John is love,
specifically authentic love. How many of you knew I was going to say that? That
means some of you were paying attention to the readings. This was meant for the
times when it was written, and the cure is meant for our times today. A cure to
divisiveness and spiritual abuse is love. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Yes, a cure to these ills, I submit, is love and caring.
That is God tells us to be love, to be love authentically and with whole-heart
– no matter where they are on life’s journey, whether they are believers, what
they say, or how they live their lives. We are love now and always. From a
pastoral care perspective, this makes sense because people often come to me
with a list of issues and many of the issues are about what other people are
doing --as in what they are doing or not doing – or at least what they think is
happening.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span>Just because you may not see
someone pray might also mean they might be taking the Gospel of Matthew to
heart about not praying in public or loud. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
In that list of who and what, their focus is upon someone
else and how those people irritate or offended them. To clarify, there are
legitimate and real pains because of damage done. Jesus tells us that judgment
coming, but that is not our call. We take care to correct our own paths and our
response to injustice. Do we enact pain upon someone else because we are in
pain? No. Do we allow people to continue injustice upon us? No. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Do we look with faith for the love of Jesus? Are we love?<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
The letter from John teaches us not just to be love but why
it is so important. In the words of 1<sup>st</sup> John, love casts out fear
and punishment. That is precisely because there is no reason to fear when you
walk with love. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Isn’t that really the crux of the issue with spiritual abuse
and divisiveness is fear? Instead of trying to understand another person or how
they come to God, fear is used to mask and to avoid the opportunity to
transform each of us. Essentially, we have allowed fear to paralyze our society
into this sickness.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
That fear is for us to prune away and toss away as withered
and rejected branches because that will not bear the fruit our community needs.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Beloved: be love and love all brothers and sisters. Don’t
let fear win.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
We have called it by name and we have a cure.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Like any great journey, there is a path to the cure.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<b style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal;">A Path: <o:p></o:p></b></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
A path is the challenge for us. As a gardener, I especially
resonate with a Gospel story that talks about growing fruits and vines. Partially,
I can enjoy the results as a snack or meal, but I know that growing a garden of
flowers, herbs and fruit is hard work. It takes some discipline. Some days the
discipline is great and some days, I am flat lazy. In those days, I have to pay
more attention and really pull together the effort to keep going. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
So yes, when the Gospel mentions growing gardens and vines,
I am there! Hopefully, I can learn a tip or two along the way (like soil depths
or proper shading). The tips from Jesus are kind of like the nuts and bolts of
gardening, and that we have to tend all parts of the garden or the vine or else
we risk losing parts of it. That is figuratively speaking how we have to tend
to all parts of the community to be His Church. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
(Even Paul’s letters to Corinth reminds us too that our
Church requires all parts of the Body or the Church.) From my experience, it is
nearly impossible to grow a fruit that is detached from its root or vine.
Unlike the vine or grape, people can be reconnected and help the whole
community grow together. Together, we help the whole grow because we know that
poor conditions can impact the wider connectedness. How can we help those? We
raise the conditions and give them attention. The answer is love!<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Thus, despite the spiritual abuse from social media, news,
or certain misguided ones, we have an opportunity to repair damage and grow our
community again. As I said before (and in the Gospels, we do this through
action, sharing and engaging our community with that cure.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
The cure and path can be tricky because this does not come
with instant gratification or allow for easy judgments. Our path may not seem
easy to market or sell because it requires dedication to love, discipline to
open ourselves, and willingness to invite people into our lives that we may not
normally invite.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Yes, we invite them with all of their brokenness so that we
can learn from each other. As difficult as that may sound, the payoff can be
immense and shines. When we show our love by engaging our community and
supporting all of God’s Beloved children, we will see a community that rises,
takes care of each other, shakes hands with each other, has coffee together,
and sings praises together. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
We don’t need division and hurt. We don’t need fear. We know
what is making us sick, we know the cure and is our Church’s mission from Jesus
to our community and our posterity that we pursue this path. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
You don’t get to the cure by pointing fingers and trying to
look superior. No one is perfect and no one is exempt from God’s love. We
cannot start being the cure by being that which we are trying to cure. There is
enough division in our world without us reinforcing our own.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
We know the name, we have a cure and it is up to us to do
the therapy to get better. So our path is to start today in the fellowship hall
after worship because we are not just here for words; we are here for action as
an action-oriented, mission-based Church. There are a couple action plans in
mind, but let’s hear your action plan. A discussion series is being offered to
discuss the issue in depth along with reviewing a book to initiate a healthy
dialogue for those that want to study the issue more. <span style="mso-spacerun: yes;"> </span>If you want to help in our community outreach
efforts, you wont want to miss these chances. <o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
There is so much that we can do and so much that we must do.
It is up to us to live out the example we have been given by Jesus and teach
the world (our community) as God’s community. Our community needs this and God
wants this. We teach them what love looks like by being love and by welcoming all
Beloved of God.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
It won’t be easy because good fruit on the vine does not
just happen because we say it does. That takes time, work, attention, and
loving care. We do our part and be a great example. Remind ourselves to leave
room for people to join us, for ideas and for God’s big love to embrace us all.
We are going to do some wonderful work.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
We do that by being the best UCC can be.<span style="mso-spacerun: yes;">  </span><o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
That is how we bear fruit for generations and stay connected
to our community.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
We are love in thoughts, words and action because love wins.<o:p></o:p></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
<br /></div>
<div class="MsoNormal">
Thanks Be to God.<o:p></o:p></div>
<!--EndFragment--><br /></div>

posts.title: Where Do You Belong? - John 10, Psalm 23
posts.author: Tony E Hansen
posts.summary: Psalm 23, John 10:11-18, and 1 John 3:16-24 invite us to consider where we truly belong. The sermon explores Christ as the Good Shepherd whose call to service draws us into community, challenging us with the discomfort that faithful discipleship requires.
